# A Canadian book with a US dollar bank below zero and a US dollar card above
# zero, each reached twice with a figure in Canadian dollars.
#
# Assets:USD Bank pays 100.00 USD of travel at 1.30 while it holds nothing,
# then 200.00 USD more at 1.35. It goes from 0 to -100.00 and then to -300.00,
# acting as a liability, so each payment opens a liability cost basis on the
# bank's split: 100.00 USD owed at 1.30 and 200.00 USD owed at 1.35.
#
# Liabilities:USD Card is charged 100.00 USD of travel at 1.30, which opens a
# liability cost basis of 100.00 USD owed at 1.30. It is then paid 300.00 USD
# from the Canadian bank at 1.35. That repays the 100.00 it owed, drawing on
# the charge's cost basis, and takes the card from 0 to +200.00, acting as an
# asset, so the payment's split opens an asset cost basis of 200.00 USD held
# at 1.35. It is paid 100.00 USD more at 1.40, from +200.00 to +300.00, which
# opens a second asset cost basis of 100.00 USD held at 1.40.
#
# What this fixture produces: Assets:USD Bank at -300.00 USD with two
# liability cost bases, 100.00 and 200.00; Liabilities:USD Card at +300.00 USD
# with an asset cost basis of 200.00 and one of 100.00; and the charge's
# liability cost basis drawn to nothing.
#
# Verified by
# tests/scenario/test_every_cost_basis_is_consumable_on_its_own_side_and_never_below_nothing.py.
2034-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2034-01-01 commodity USD
	mnemonic: "USD"
	fullname: "US Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
